name: ObjectBox
tagline: Fast on-device object database with built-in HNSW vector search and an optional commercial sync server.
description: ObjectBox is an embedded object database for mobile, desktop and IoT devices, with bindings for Java/Kotlin, Dart/Flutter, Swift, C/C++, Go and Python. You annotate entity classes and get ACID transactions, relations and indexed queries without an ORM. Since version 4 it also ships an on-device HNSW vector index, which makes it one of the few practical options for local RAG or semantic search on phones. Data sync to other devices or a self-hosted server is a separate commercial product, ObjectBox Sync, which the company now markets as an Atlas Device Sync replacement.

license.name: Free closed-source core; Apache-2.0 language bindings

pricing.notes: The database is free to use. ObjectBox Sync (device-to-server and peer sync) is licensed commercially.

scale.notes: Single-process embedded store; scale-out only via ObjectBox Sync replicas.

strengths: On-device HNSW vector index for local semantic search and RAG
Very low per-operation overhead; benchmarks well against SQLite-based ORMs on mobile
Same object API on Android, iOS, Flutter, Linux, Windows and embedded C
Automatic schema handling for most model changes without hand-written migrations
weaknesses: Core engine is closed source; only the bindings are on GitHub
Sync is a paid add-on rather than part of the free product
No SQL; complex aggregation and reporting must be done in application code
useCases: On-device AI features needing local vector search
IoT gateways and embedded Linux devices
Replacing Realm after the Device Sync shutdown
notIdealFor: Teams that require a fully open-source stack
